notes:
First attempt succeeded (200), no retries needed, attempts[] is empty. No status:0 / hang observed — the v2 tier was reachable for this write, consistent with the sibling create call working earlier.

*** THE HEADLINE TEST — RESOLVED: THE GUIDANCE TEXT IS WRONG. CREATE AND UPDATE AGREE. ***
This capability's own declared guidance says: 'Making an option the default does not clear the previous default; on a single-select dropdown clear the old one yourself.' That is false, measured directly.

Before this call: 146670 was the live default (is_default:true), 146669 and 146668 were both false.
The call sent ONLY option_id=146669 with option_value unchanged and is_default:true. It never named 146670 anywhere in path or body.
Reading all three options back afterward (not trusting the write response) shows:
  - 146669: is_default:true (as sent) — updated_at bumped to 2026-09-22T05:23:42.000Z
  - 146670: is_default:**false** — silently flipped, updated_at bumped to the SAME 2026-09-22T05:23:42.000Z, i.e. mutated in the same request as a side effect
  - 146668: untouched — still is_default:false, updated_at still 2026-09-21T13:47:13.000Z (unchanged from before this call)
So the outcome is outcome #1 from the task's three possibilities: 146670 was auto-demoted. Only one option is ever default at a time; nobody ends up with two defaults. This UPDATE path enforces single-default exactly the same way the CREATE path was observed to (creating 146670 with is_default:true had silently demoted 146668 in the earlier probe). The two sibling write calls do NOT have different default-demotion semantics — they agree with each other and disagree with this capability's own authored guidance. Verdict is DRIFT on that basis: the declared behavioral contract (guidance text) contradicts the measured behavior, even though the response *schema* itself was a clean match (see below) — this is a guidance/behavior drift, not a shape drift.

*** RESPONSE SCHEMA — CLEAN MATCH, SEPARATE FROM THE GUIDANCE DRIFT ***
The 200 body was exactly {success:true, data:{id, option_value, is_default, colour, parent_option_id}} — every declared key present (id:146669, option_value echoed verbatim, is_default:true as sent, colour:null, parent_option_id:null), nothing undeclared. declared_missing and undeclared_returned are both empty. If judged purely on response shape this would be a PASS; the DRIFT verdict here is specifically about the guidance-vs-behavior contradiction, which is the more consequential defect and the reason this probe was run.

*** PARTIAL-UPDATE FIELD PRESERVATION — CONFIRMED ***
colour and parent_option_id are not accepted as body params by this capability at all (only option_value and is_default are declared, both required). Read-back confirms both stayed exactly as they were (colour:null, parent_option_id:null on 146669, unchanged) — not because the handler merges fields, but because it structurally cannot touch them. option_value was resent unchanged and round-tripped unchanged. This is a full replace of a two-field subset, not a partial-fields-omitted-preserved semantics; there's no way to test 'omit option_value and see if it's preserved' because omitting it is a 400 per the declared guidance (not attempted here, matches contract, not retried).

*** DUPLICATE-OPTION CHECK — FIFTH INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION ***
get_custom_field_dataset_v2(fetch_options=true) after the update still shows exactly 3 rows (info.count:3), ids 146670/146669/146668 each appearing exactly once. Combined with the four prior confirmations logged against the create-path siblings (field-definition-create, dataset-create, single-option-create via two read paths), this is a fifth independent read confirming new/updated custom-field options never double — the historical duplication seen on the old default fields (priority/status/case_type) is confirmed, again, as legacy data rather than a live serializer defect anywhere on this surface.

*** THIN-WRITE vs FULL-READ DISCRIMINATOR — CONFIRMED AGAIN ***
The update's own 200 response (id, option_value, is_default, colour, parent_option_id) does not carry record_status/created_at/updated_at/dataset_id — deliberately thin, matching the declared schema exactly. Reading the same option back through get_custom_field_dataset_v2 shows the full stored row for 146669: {id:146669, group_id:3452, project_id:null, custom_field_id:106131, dataset_id:31320, option_value:'__mcp-probe-cfdataset-20260921-B', is_default:true, parent_option_id:null, record_status:'active', created_at:'2026-09-21T13:34:12.000Z', updated_at:'2026-09-22T05:23:42.000Z'}. Same pattern as the create-path sibling: write response thin, read carries everything, and updated_at moved while created_at did not — consistent with an in-place update rather than a delete+recreate.

*** ADJACENT DRIFT NOTED (not this capability's contract, flagged for completeness) ***
get_custom_field_dataset_v2's own declared 200 schema lists `options` as a plain array; the actual response nests it as `options.data` (array) plus an `options.info` paging envelope ({page, page_size, count, prev, next}) that isn't declared anywhere on that capability. This didn't block reading back this probe's results (the array was found one level deeper than declared) but is a genuine shape mismatch on the READ sibling, separate from and additional to the guidance-drift found on update_custom_field_dataset_option_v2 itself.
